WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE COMING FROM E AT 16 KTS WHICH ALIGNED WELL WITH THE ORIENTATION OF THE SLICKS. UNCERTAINTIES: THE POINT SOURCE WAS UNKNOWN BUT THERE WERE VARIOUS OIL WELLS WITHIN THE VICINITY.

properties.content:

Nearest City: Cameron, WV

Incident Type: FIXED
Material: OIL, MISC: MINERAL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: AEP WHEELING POWER COMPANY
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 39.924444, -80.550278 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 12 gallons
Report Description
A UTILITY POLE WAS BROKEN DURING A SEVERE THUNDER STORM. THE TRANSFORMER ATTACHED TO THE POLE WAS DAMAGED WHEN THE POLE TOP HIT THE GROUND. THE TRANSFORMER RELEASED APPROXIMATELY 10 TO 12 GALLONS OF OIL. THE TRANSFORMER IS A 25KVA CENTRAL MOLONEY UNIT MANUFACTURED IN 1976. WE ARE TREATING THIS OIL AS "ASSUMED" PCB-CONTAMINATED. THE SPILL SITE WAS FIRST DISCOVERED AT APPROXIMATELY 1040 HRS. IT WAS NOT UNTIL APPROXIMATELY 1430 HRS THAT AN OIL SHEEN WAS OBSERVED IN A SMALL CREEK LOCATED NEAR THE SPILL SITE. SUNPRO, A SPILL CLEANUP CONTRACTOR HAS BEEN CALLED IN TO ASSIST US WITH THE CLEANUP OF THIS SPILL EVENT.
